Solids keep their shape and volume. Liquids keep their volume but take their container's shape. Gases have no fixed shape or volume and fill their container. It is important to look carefully and record observations in notebooks because science has a long history. However, solid particles are widely spaced and move freely throughout a container, liquid particles are immobile and locked together, and gas particles are tightly packed and only vibrate in place. This is why gases cannot be compressed, while solids are easy to compress like air. Famous scientists have studied nature for centuries, and these ideas affect technology, cooking, sports, and daily life.
